claims.text: Not being mapped to the previous Special Intensive Revision (SIR) accounted for 42% of the notices issued to voters on Delhi's draft electoral roll.
Name mismatches with the previous electoral roll accounted for 41% of SIR notices issued in Delhi, with parent name mismatches comprising 24% and self-name mismatches comprising 17%.
Discrepancies in age differences accounted for 16% of the SIR notices issued in Delhi.
A total of 59,791 SIR notices issued to voters in Delhi had no reason listed against them.
Shyam Mukhija, aged 125 from Sadar Bazar assembly constituency in Old Delhi, was the oldest person served an SIR notice due to a self-name mismatch.
Notices were issued to 34.5% of men, 33.4% of women, and 50% of transgender individuals on Delhi's draft electoral roll.
More than 80.62 lakh voter names were deleted from draft rolls after being marked as shifted or absent, but only 6.66 lakh Form-6 applications were submitted for inclusion.
During the SIR process in Bihar, the total electorate decreased from 7.89 crore to about 7.42 crore despite 21.53 lakh electors being added through Form-6 applications.
Prominent political and official figures served SIR notices in Delhi include LK Advani, Jagdeep Dhankhar, S Jaishankar, Sukhbir Singh Sandhu, Manish Sisodia, and Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta.
Deceased former chairman of the Economic Advisory Council to the Prime Minister Bibek Debroy was issued an SIR notice as his name appeared on the flagged draft rolls.
The Delhi Chief Electoral Officer's office stated that disposal of notices will be completed by October 29, 2026, and the final electoral roll will be published on November 4, 2026.
Lawyer Kapil Sibal described the Special Intensive Revision as a 'special intensive deletion' aimed at removing valid voters.
The Election Commission of India launched the Special Intensive Revision exercise in Delhi on May 14.
Authorities in Delhi received 84,263 Form-6 applications for voter inclusion between August 31 and September 19, following 2,12,400 applications received up to August 30.
Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta was issued an SIR notice because the age difference between her and her parents appeared to be under 15 years.
Former Supreme Court judge Justice Madan B Lokur received an SIR notice because the age gap between him and his grandfather was recorded as 40 years or less.
Delhi is among 19 states and Union Territories included in the third phase of the Special Intensive Revision voter roll process.
The director of IIT Kharagpur sent a message reminding students that their admission to the institute serves as evidence of sustained effort.
The Mumbai Police transferred the investigation into the death of an IIT Bombay student to the Crime Branch, to be led by an Assistant Commissioner of Police.
Sahil, a second-year IIT Bombay student, was found dead in his hostel room after an invigilating professor reported him for possessing a phone during an examination.
Sahil's father filed an FIR against Professor Suryanarayana Doolla under the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, alleging three months of harassment.
The Faculty Forum of IIT Bombay defended Professor Suryanarayana Doolla, stating he was executing institute-approved procedures during exam invigilation.
IIT Bombay Director Shireesh Kedare denied allegations of caste-based discrimination, stating student caste information remains confidential from faculty and administrators.
Sahil Wakode, a 20-year-old second-year student of energy science and engineering at IIT Bombay, died by suicide in the third such case on the campus this year.
IIT Bombay Director Shireesh Kedare signed a document agreeing to 18 demands presented by protesting students during a late-night meeting at the campus gate.
Protesting students demanded the suspension of Professor Suryanarayana Doolla, an open apology, an independent probe committee, and faculty sensitisation.
IIT Bombay planned to replace ceiling fans with wall-mounted fans in student hostels as a preventive safety measure following recent suicides.
Mumbai Police registered an FIR charging Professor Suryanarayan Doolla and unidentified persons with abetment to suicide and violations of the SC/ST Act.
IIT Bombay stated that Sahil Wakode was caught using a mobile phone to upload an exam question paper onto the ChatGPT AI chatbot.
Sahil Wakode's family refused to claim his body from Rajawadi Hospital for seven hours until police assured them the case was transferred to the Crime Branch.
